key_insight: SpikeDS uses dual sparsity in a spiking transformer to focus computation on the most informative 3D MRI regions for predicting perineural invasion in cholangiocarcinoma.
clinical_relevance: If validated further, this approach could improve risk stratification from volumetric MRI while reducing the energy and compute burden of 3D AI models.
method: Binary spiking communication for activation sparsity
Window pruning guided by firing rates to skip low-salience regions
Cross-window attention to keep global context even when some windows are pruned
evidence_signal: In 139 cholangiocarcinoma patients with 5-fold cross-validation, SpikeDS reached an AUC of 0.753 and used 14.4 mJ, outperforming the strongest baseline on both accuracy and energy efficiency.
watch_item: Results come from a single-cohort retrospective evaluation, so external validation is needed before clinical deployment.
paper_title: SpikeDS: Dual Sparsity Spikformer for Perineural Invasion Prediction in 3D MRI
